newsitem.title: USA: Zinc stocks to shrink further in 1997 - Metaleurop.
newsitem.headline: Zinc stocks to shrink further in 1997 - Metaleurop.

text.p: Zinc stocks will drop further as market participants buy material from London Metal Exhange warehouses because of concentrates shortfalls, Christian Bue, board member of Metaleurop said.
"Stocks of zinc will go down further this year. Logically, as a consequence of the concentrates situation, a number of players will have to buy from the LME stocks," Bue told reporters.
The annual American Zinc Association's four day meeting here ended today.

In a presentation earlier this week by Cominco, the Canadian miner and smelter, the company's president and ceo, David Thompson said it may have to buy 50,000 tonnes of zinc off the LME stocks this year to meet strong demand.
The zinc concentrates market has tightened, with some analysts forecasting a small deficit this year which may cause some cutbacks in refined metal output at certain smelters, particularly in Europe.
Earlier on Wednesday Metaleurop, one of the world's biggest zinc smelters agreed on a benchmark deal for concentrates bought from Cominco.

Bue said since the initial 110,000 tonnes of concentrates deal was concluded at a mid-point range of $186 per tonne basis LME cash zinc price of $1,100 per tonne, Metaleurop has booked two other deals at similar levels with other mining companies.
